title: The Corporal, the Ministry and the River: José López Rega from the Palacio Unzué to Chacarita
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth on a contested day
stops.date_confidence: the year 1916 is agreed. es.wikipedia gives 17 October, en.wikipedia gives 17 November; neither cites the civil register. October is carried, November is recorded as the rival reading and not set aside
stops.campa: A son is born in Buenos Aires to Juan López and Manuela Rega, Spanish immigrants, and the mother dies in or just after the birth. No document reachable in this run names the street or the parish. The press chronicle that puts the house in Bajo Belgrano is chronicle and not register, and it is left outside the file. He will spend seventy-two years in this city, leave it twice, and come back the second time on a plane paid for by the government that wants him. The day of the birth is itself in dispute.
suggested_refs: The civil register of the City of Buenos Aires for November and October 1916, not consulted, which would settle the birth date

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the marriage and the badge
stops.date_confidence: 19 June 1943 attested for the marriage and 17 February 1945 for the daughter; the entry into the Policía Federal is dated only to shortly afterward
stops.campa: He marries Josefa Flora Maseda Fontenla in June and enters the Policía Federal Argentina soon after, sponsored by comisario Filomeno Velazco. A daughter, Norma Beatriz, is born in February 1945. Eight months later a colonel named Juan Perón is carried out of Martín García and into the Plaza de Mayo by a crowd, and the country the new agent will police for the next twenty years takes the shape it keeps. He is a patrolman. He will retire one rank above the place where he starts.
suggested_refs: The service file of agent José López Rega, Policía Federal Argentina, 1943-1962, not reachable

stops.name: Palacio Unzué, the guard at the president's door
stops.date_confidence: 1951 attested for joining the presidential guard; no month or day recorded, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: He joins the guard at the presidential residence standing between avenida del Libertador, Austria, Agüero and Las Heras. Juan Perón is in his first term and Eva Perón is dying upstairs in the house. The agent on the door has no part in any of it and is close enough to hear the doctors come and go. The palace is pulled down in 1958 and the Biblioteca Nacional is built on the ground, so this pin marks an absence. Twenty-three years later he decides who enters the president's room.
suggested_refs: The site of the Palacio Unzué, demolished 1958, now occupied by the Biblioteca Nacional

stops.name: Paso de los Libres, the house of Doña Victoria
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia dates the Radio Nacional singing to 1951 and the Villone introduction to the years following, without a year for the visit itself; 1955 is a placeholder inside the 1950s
stops.campa: The journalist José María Villone, who met him after hearing him sing on Radio Nacional, takes him to a house on the Brazilian border where a woman known only as Doña Victoria leads a rosicrucian circle called the Fraternidad Antigua. There he learns the syncretism that fills his later books: zodiac, karma, colors, plants, music, the reincarnating soul. He is a serving police officer with a wife, a daughter and a beat. The Argentine press will call this brujería. He will call it knowledge.
suggested_refs: The rosicrucian circle Fraternidad Antigua at Paso de los Libres, Corrientes, on the Brazilian frontier

stops.name: Panama City, the cabaret that may never have happened
stops.date_confidence: the legend itself is undated; c. 1955 is the range in which the press usually places it. Recorded as tradition, not as event, and contradicted by the encyclopedic account of a first meeting at Buenos Aires in 1966
stops.campa: A version repeated for fifty years in the Argentine press has the policeman meeting a dancer named María Estela Martínez in a Panama City cabaret, years before either of them matters to anyone. No consulted encyclopedic source carries it, and it contradicts the version those sources do carry, which puts the first meeting in a Buenos Aires living room in 1966. The pin stands because the legend is part of the life whether or not the meeting is.
suggested_refs: The recurrent Argentine press tradition on the Panamanian origin of Isabel Perón, unconfirmed in es.wikipedia
sources: recurrent journalistic tradition, not confirmed in es.wikipedia.org, 'José López Rega' or 'Isabel Martínez de Perón'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, retirement at the rank of cabo primero
stops.date_confidence: 1962 attested for the retirement and the rank; no month or day recorded, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: He leaves the Policía Federal Argentina after nearly twenty years with the rank of cabo primero, first-class corporal, one step above the bottom of a scale with a dozen steps in it. Nothing in the record says why he goes. He is forty-six. In May 1974 he will be promoted from this rank to Comisario General, the top of the same scale, without passing through anything in between, by a president who owes him her office. The twelve years between the two ranks are spent publishing horoscopes.
suggested_refs: The rank ladder of the Policía Federal Argentina, from cabo primero to Comisario General

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Astrología Esotérica and the name El Brujo
stops.date_confidence: 1962 attested for publication; no month recorded, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: He publishes Astrología Esotérica: secretos develados, which ties the signs of the zodiac to colors, plants and music. The reviews are devastating, and es.wikipedia reports that the nickname El Brujo comes out of them: the press hands him the name in derision, eleven years before the derided man runs a ministry. No review is cited by name in any source reachable here, so the origin of the name is report and not document, and the file keeps that distinction.
suggested_refs: José López Rega, Astrología Esotérica: secretos develados (Buenos Aires, 1962)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Alfa y Omega and the Astroagenda
stops.date_confidence: 1963 and 1965 attested for the two titles, no months recorded. El Sabio Hindú is dated 1972 in one line of the same article and 1977 in another; the contradiction is not adjudicated
stops.campa: Alfa y Omega: un mensaje para la humanidad appears in 1963, on esotericism, karma and reincarnation, and La Astroagenda in 1965, a day-by-day horoscope for the coming year. A later mystical narrative, El Sabio Hindú, is dated 1972 in one line of the same article and 1977 in another. No translation into any language is documented and no re-edition after his fall is found. The books are the instrument by which a retired corporal becomes a man that people in politics ask to see.
suggested_refs: José López Rega, Alfa y Omega (1963), La Astroagenda (1965), El Sabio Hindú (1972 or 1977)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the house of Bernardo Alberte
stops.date_confidence: the corpus dates the introduction 1 May 1966; es.wikipedia places it inside Isabel's 1965-66 stay without a day. A rival account gives 1965 through the Logia Anael, and press tradition gives Panama c. 1955. None of the three is set aside
stops.campa: In the house of Lieutenant Colonel Bernardo Alberte, Isabel Martínez de Perón, in Argentina for eight months as her husband's personal delegate against the neo-Peronists, hears the astrologer speak and asks for a private meeting. She offers him work as her secretary in Madrid. He is fifty and has published four books nobody in government has read. She is thirty-five and has never held an office. Two months later he is living in Juan Perón's house. The room where she hires him has no documented address.
suggested_refs: isabel_peron.journey.json, stop dated 1966-05-01, the introduction at Bernardo Alberte's house

stops.name: Puerta de Hierro, the household absorbs the secretary
stops.date_confidence: 9 July 1966 attested in the corpus for the flight to Madrid; en.wikipedia runs the Madrid period from 1965, es.wikipedia dates his relocation back to Argentina to 1971. The ends of the period are not reconciled
stops.campa: On Argentine independence day he flies to Madrid in the seat beside Isabel Perón and enters the villa that has already held Juan Perón's eighteen years of exile and will hold Eva Perón's returned coffin. He arrives as her secretary and becomes the general's private secretary, her bodyguard, and the man who decides which envoy from Buenos Aires gets an hour. He will not leave this address until Argentina is ready to receive it whole.
suggested_refs: The quinta 17 de Octubre at the Ciudad Residencial Puerta de Hierro, Madrid; note that the coordinate often given for Puerta de Hierro is the gate monument, some two kilometres south-southeast

stops.name: Puerta de Hierro, the coffin from Milan
stops.date_confidence: 3 September 1971 attested in the corpus for the arrival of the body at Madrid; en.wikipedia dates the exhumation and flight to Spain to 1971
stops.campa: The embalmed body of Eva Perón, buried under a false name in Milan for fourteen years, is exhumed and delivered to the house in Madrid. Juan Perón keeps it in the dining room on a platform near the table. Isabel Perón combs its hair, dresses it, talks to it as though it can hear her. The secretary who arrived five years ago is now the household's authority on what the dead require, the man who claims to know what rites a body like this one needs and how long they take.
suggested_refs: eva_peron.journey.json and isabel_peron.journey.json, the Puerta de Hierro coffin stops of September 1971

stops.name: Puerta de Hierro, the rites over the two women
stops.date_confidence: no date is recorded for any ritual. The commonly repeated 1960s dating is impossible: the corpse reached Madrid in 1971 and left for Argentina in 1974, and he relocated to Buenos Aires in 1973. 1972 is the midpoint of the only possible window
stops.campa: Tradition holds that in this house he works rites over the open coffin and over the living wife at once, to pass the spirit of the first Peronist saint into the third Peronist wife. No primary source is cited for it in any article consulted; the story is old, general and everywhere at once. What can be dated is the window. The body arrives in 1971 and leaves for Argentina in 1974, and he himself moves to Buenos Aires in 1973. The English accounts that put the rites in the 1960s put them before the coffin exists in Madrid.
suggested_refs: The transfer-of-spirit tradition attached to the Madrid household, uncited in every consulted encyclopedic article
sources: en.wikipedia.org, 'Eva Perón' (for the 1971 arrival and 1974 return that bound the window)

stops.name: Rome, the lodge of Licio Gelli
stops.date_confidence: February 1973 attested for the P2 affiliation; no day recorded, defaulted to 01. The lodge premises are not specified in the source
stops.campa: He is received into Propaganda Due, the masonic lodge Licio Gelli runs out of Italy, weeks before Peronism returns to power in Argentina and while the lodge is looking for reach into the government that is coming. Thirteen years later Gelli's network is what keeps a wanted man in a Rome apartment out of the hands of an Argentine junta. He is fifty-six, a private astrologer with no office, three months away from a ministry. Nothing in the source says what he did in the lodge or who proposed him.
suggested_refs: The membership lists of Propaganda Due, surfaced in Italy in 1981

stops.name: Beijing, the mission of the movement
stops.date_confidence: the mission is dated 8 to 18 May 1973 in the corpus; es.wikipedia dates it only to May 1973
stops.campa: He flies to the People's Republic of China with Isabel Perón on a mission of the Peronist movement, ten days before Héctor Cámpora is sworn in at Buenos Aires. The delegation is a wife with no office and her secretary, carrying an exiled general's authority into a state that has only just begun receiving the West. The Argentine right he will arm within the year regards China as the enemy in the abstract. He shakes hands and goes on to the next capital.
suggested_refs: isabel_peron.journey.json, stop dated 1973-05-08, the Beijing mission

stops.name: Pyongyang, Kim Il-sung receives the delegation
stops.date_confidence: attested to the 8-18 May 1973 mission; the exact day at Pyongyang is not recorded and 15 is the placeholder the corpus already uses
stops.campa: The mission continues to North Korea and Kim Il-sung receives Isabel Perón with her secretary standing behind her. Within four days of this handshake he holds an Argentine ministry, and within three months he is organizing killings out of it. The sources reachable here give the itinerary of the Asian trip and not one word of what was said in either capital. It is a documented journey with no documented content, and the file records the hole rather than filling it.
suggested_refs: isabel_peron.journey.json, stop dated 1973-05-15, Kim Il-sung receives the delegation

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Minister of Social Welfare
stops.date_confidence: 25 May 1973 for both the inauguration and the appointment, agreed by both encyclopedias. The 11 March 1973 date that circulates is the election day, not the inauguration; the working notes for this file carried that error and it is corrected here
stops.campa: Héctor Cámpora takes office after eighteen years of Peronist proscription and Perón places his secretary in the Ministry of Social Welfare. He will hold it under Cámpora, under Raúl Lastiri, under Perón himself and under Isabel Perón: four presidents, one desk, twenty-five months. The ministry pays pensions, runs housing and buys medicine. Its budget is larger than most provinces and almost nobody audits it, and within the year it is paying the salaries and the fuel of the Alianza Anticomunista Argentina.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Héctor José Cámpora', for the 11 March election and 25 May inauguration dates

stops.name: Ezeiza, the massacre at the platform
stops.date_confidence: 20 June 1973 attested for the massacre in both encyclopedias; his personal direction of the shooters is described in both as an allegation and is carried here as one
stops.campa: Between one and three million people come to the airport to meet Perón coming home for good. Gunmen of the Peronist right, positioned at and around the speakers' platform, open fire on the Montonero columns approaching it. The dead are counted in dozens and the wounded in hundreds. Both encyclopedias say the minister organized the operation and both say allegedly, and nobody consulted here says it without the word.
suggested_refs: The speakers' platform at the Ezeiza bridge, 20 June 1973

stops.name: Morón Air Base, the homecoming diverted
stops.date_confidence: 20 June 1973 attested for the diversion in the corpus and in es.wikipedia, 'Masacre de Ezeiza'
stops.campa: The aircraft carrying Perón, Isabel Perón and the minister is turned away from Ezeiza and put down on a military runway at Morón instead, under army guard, while the crowd assembled for the return goes on shooting at itself twenty kilometres away. Eighteen years of exile end on tarmac. The man who came out of the Madrid household as a secretary walks off the plane as a minister of the Argentine state, and the first act of the restored movement is a massacre of its own left.
suggested_refs: isabel_peron.journey.json, stop dated 1973-06-20, Morón air base

stops.name: Teatro Colón, the Perón-Perón ticket
stops.date_confidence: 5 August 1973 attested for the proclamation and 23 September 1973 for the election at 61.85 percent
stops.campa: The movement proclaims the ticket at the opera house: the general for president, his third wife for vice president, over the objection of half his lieutenants and of every faction that expected second place for itself. The minister has pushed for her place harder than anyone. On the twenty-third of September the ticket takes 61.85 percent, the largest mandate in Argentine electoral history. He has been elected to nothing. He has arranged a line of succession, and the man at the head of it is seventy-seven and ill.
suggested_refs: isabel_peron.journey.json, stop dated 1973-08-05, the proclamation at the Teatro Colón

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the state of war against the infiltrators
stops.date_confidence: 1 October 1973 attested for the Superior Council declaration; the Benítez statement quoted here is undated in the source
stops.campa: The Peronist Superior Council declares a state of war against Marxist infiltrators inside the movement. The declaration is public, signed and printed, and it is the license. Six weeks later the first bomb goes off under a senator's car. For two years the Interior Ministry will answer every question about the killings with one sentence, while the organization doing the killing draws police cars and state fuel from a building eight blocks from the Casa Rosada.
stops.quote: Al gobierno no le consta la existencia de la Triple A.
stops.quote_source: Antonio Benítez, Minister of the Interior, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Alianza Anticomunista Argentina'
suggested_refs: The declaration of the Consejo Superior Peronista, 1 October 1973

stops.name: Avenida Hipólito Yrigoyen 370, the ministry and the Alliance
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia gives 13 July 1973 as the founding date of the Alliance; es.wikipedia gives an undated 1973 organizing period beginning after the ministerial appointment. 1 July is the file's placeholder inside the disputed window and the precise July date is not treated as established
stops.campa: From this building he runs pensions, housing and the Alianza Anticomunista Argentina at the same time. Rodolfo Almirón commands the guns and comisario Alberto Villar brings the police. The organization draws vehicles, fuel and salaries from the ministry that pays for the country's poor. A weapons store inside the building is attested only from its discovery in July 1975; the microcine detail that circulates in the working notes is not in the ministry's own article and is dropped.
stops.quote: No le dé pelota a ese loco, usted limítese a aplicar la ley
stops.quote_source: Juan Domingo Perón, on López Rega pressing him about death squads, reported by Miguel Ángel Iñíguez in a 1986 interview, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Alianza Anticomunista Argentina'
suggested_refs: The Ministerio de Bienestar Social building, Avenida Hipólito Yrigoyen 370, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the bomb in the senator's car
stops.date_confidence: 21 November 1973 attested. The working notes framed this as an attack on his home; the source describes a bomb placed in his vehicle, and his own article records two Triple A attempts, 1973 and 1975
stops.campa: A bomb placed in the vehicle of the radical senator Hipólito Solari Yrigoyen goes off and wounds him in the legs. It is the first attack the Alliance signs with its own three letters, six days before the commando at San Miguel station. He survives it and survives a second attempt in 1975. An organization that has been working unnamed since the winter now announces that it exists, in the same weeks in which the government begins saying, and goes on saying, that it does not.
suggested_refs: The 21 November 1973 car bombing of senator Hipólito Solari Yrigoyen, first signed action of the Alliance

stops.name: San Miguel, the attack at the station
stops.date_confidence: 27 November 1973 attested in es.wikipedia, 'Triple A (Argentina)'
stops.campa: Six days after the senator's car, a commando attacks Antonio Deleroni and Nélida Arana at the San Miguel station on the General San Martín line, in the western suburbs. Two names on a list that will run to somewhere between seven hundred and fifteen hundred, depending on which article of the same encyclopedia is open. The Alliance works outward from the capital along the commuter rails: teachers, priests, lawyers, students, union delegates, taken at their doors and at their stops.
suggested_refs: Estación San Miguel, línea General San Martín, attack of 27 November 1973

stops.name: Tripoli, the errand to Libya
stops.date_confidence: 1974 attested for the trip; no month or day recorded, defaulted to 01-01, and no agenda, interlocutor or result is given in any consulted source
stops.campa: He travels to Libya representing the Argentine government. The sources reachable here give the destination and the year and nothing further: no agenda, no interlocutor, no result, no date inside the year. It is recorded because it happened and left open because that is the state of the record. A minister of social welfare with a private army and an astrological practice is in Tripoli in 1974, and no source reached here can say what for. What is documented at both ends of the trip is the killing at home, which does not pause for it.
suggested_refs: The Argentine diplomatic record of the 1974 Libyan mission, not reachable

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Comisario General in one step
stops.date_confidence: 3 May 1974 attested in es.wikipedia for the promotion and for its bypassing of the intermediate ranks
stops.campa: The retired corporal is made Comisario General of the Policía Federal Argentina, the highest rank in the force, without passing through a single grade in between. He left this institution twelve years ago as a cabo primero. The promotion is signed while Juan Perón is alive and still president, and it places the man who runs an illegal death squad at the top of the rank list of the legal police that already lends it cars. Eight days later a priest is shot in Villa Luro.
suggested_refs: The 3 May 1974 promotion decree, Policía Federal Argentina

stops.name: Villa Luro, the priest at the church door
stops.date_confidence: 11 May 1974 attested, and the Alliance attribution with it. Rodolfo Almirón is named as the shooter in es.wikipedia, 'Carlos Mugica'
stops.campa: Father Carlos Mugica, priest of the villas miseria and a Peronist of the left, is shot dead leaving the church of San Francisco Solano at Zelada 4771. Rodolfo Almirón is named as the gunman. The killing is the Alliance's most public act. Almirón will be arrested for it in Spain thirty-two years later. The coordinate here is the church, not the barrio centroid that circulates in the working notes; the street address is documented and there was no need to approximate.
stops.quote: El asesinato del padre Mugica es la respuesta de Perón al retiro de ustedes en la Plaza.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Arturo Sampay, as quoted by Miguel Bonasso; cited in en.wikipedia, 'Argentine Anticommunist Alliance'
suggested_refs: The church of San Francisco Solano, calle Zelada 4771, Villa Luro, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Quinta de Olivos, the death of Perón
stops.date_confidence: 1 July 1974 attested in both encyclopedias and in the corpus. The Olivos coordinate is the corpus pin; the value in the working notes fell some nineteen kilometres west of the residence and is corrected here
stops.campa: Juan Perón dies in the early afternoon and his vice president, his third wife, assumes the presidency. The minister who arranged her place on the ticket eleven months ago is now the strongest man in the Argentine state and holds no elected office of any kind. He drafts the cabinet, controls who reaches her, and keeps the president's calendar and, according to everything written afterward, her horoscope, deciding by the stars which days are safe for her to appear in public.
suggested_refs: juan_peron.journey.json and isabel_peron.journey.json, the Olivos stops of 1 July 1974

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Villar's centurions
stops.date_confidence: the three-month peak is dated July to September 1974 in the source and 1 September is the file's placeholder inside it; Villar's assumption of operational command is dated only to 1974
stops.campa: Comisario Alberto Villar takes operational command and builds Los Centuriones inside the police, about a hundred officers drawn from federal and provincial forces and paid, in part, out of the same welfare ministry budget that funds pensions and housing. In a three-month stretch the Alliance runs some two hundred and twenty attacks, about sixty dead and forty-four seriously wounded. The historian Felipe Pigna reads the minister's posture toward the guerrilla as satisfaction.
stops.quote: un todo poderoso José López Rega que también se frota las manos frente al accionar guerrillero
stops.quote_source: Felipe Pigna, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Triple A (Argentina)', footnote 65. Note the source reads 'un todo poderoso' in two words
suggested_refs: borges.journey.json and victoria_ocampo.journey.json, the Buenos Aires stops of the 1970s

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the car bomb for Carlos Prats
stops.date_confidence: 30 September 1974 for the Prats killing as recorded in the corpus entry on the Alliance's peak year; augusto_pinochet.journey.json dates its own Condor stop to 1974 without a day
stops.campa: A car bomb kills the Chilean general Carlos Prats and his wife in this city, planted by a foreign intelligence service on Argentine soil, the exiled former commander-in-chief who had refused to back the coup against Allende. It goes off in the same weeks and the same streets in which the Alliance is running its heaviest quarter, one operation with no need to know of the other. Buenos Aires in the spring of 1974 holds two states killing in the same streets on the same nights.
suggested_refs: augusto_pinochet.journey.json, Condor segment, the Buenos Aires car bomb for Carlos Prats

stops.name: Quinta de Olivos, Eva laid beside him
stops.date_confidence: 17 November 1974 attested in the corpus for the repatriation and the laying at Olivos
stops.campa: The body he is said to have worked rites over in Madrid is brought home on the president's order and laid in a chapel at Olivos beside Juan Perón's coffin. All three are now under one roof: the founder, the saint, and the wife who governs. The man who kept the corpse company in a Madrid dining room is now the minister of the government that repatriated it, and the rites he is said to have worked over it were worked for this. Four months later his ministry begins to come apart over the price of bread.
suggested_refs: eva_peron.journey.json and isabel_peron.journey.json, the Olivos stops of 17 November 1974

stops.name: Mar del Plata, the university concentration
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia dates the CNU campaign at Mar del Plata and the Comando Libertadores de América in Córdoba to 1974-1975 without months; 1975-01-01 is the file's placeholder
stops.campa: The Concentración Nacional Universitaria, aligned with the Alliance, works this city with arson against student residences and student centres. In Córdoba the Comando Libertadores de América does the same work with police inside it. The apparatus is not one squad in the capital; it is a network of local groups with local names, sharing weapons, cars and impunity with the ministry on Hipólito Yrigoyen. The total credited to it before the coup runs between seven hundred and fifteen hundred dead, and no consulted source reconciles the two figures.
suggested_refs: The Concentración Nacional Universitaria at Mar del Plata and the Comando Libertadores de América at Córdoba, 1974-1975

segments.name: The Fall and the Ten Years' Flight

stops.name: Buenos Aires, El idioma de la verdad
stops.date_confidence: 1975 attested for publication, no month recorded, defaulted to 01-01. It precedes the 11 July resignation. The working-note framing of the book as written under exile or prison pressure is false and is struck: he was a sitting minister until July and was first detained in 1986
stops.campa: He publishes his own defense while still holding the ministry: an autobiography arguing that the press invented him. He calls the coverage of his life a saturation, and its authors sellers of information to the highest bidder, enemies of world democracy and above all enemies of the Fatherland. The book is dedicated to the Argentine people as evidence of his innocence. He is at this moment the organizer of the Alliance and the second signature in the government of Isabel Perón.
stops.quote: al pueblo argentino como testimonio de mi inocencia
stops.quote_source: José López Rega, dedication of El idioma de la verdad (1975), quoted in es.wikipedia, 'José López Rega'
suggested_refs: José López Rega, El idioma de la verdad (Buenos Aires, 1975), not consulted directly

stops.name: Casa Rosada, the resignation
stops.date_confidence: 11 July 1975 attested in both encyclopedias. The ambassadorial term runs from the resignation to 18 June 1976; the 11 May to 18 June 1975 term in the working notes appears in no consulted source and is struck
stops.campa: The Rodrigazo, the shock plan of the economy minister Celestino Rodrigo, brings the unions into the street against a Peronist government, and the price of surviving it is him. He resigns after twenty-five months and four presidents and is sent to Spain as itinerant ambassador, a title with a salary and no duties. Isabel Perón loses the man who made her and lasts eight more months without him. He is fifty-eight years old and will never hold office of any kind again.
stops.quote_source: José López Rega's phrase for press coverage of himself, El idioma de la verdad (1975), quoted in es.wikipedia, 'José López Rega'
suggested_refs: The Rodrigazo of June and July 1975 and the general strike that forced the resignation

stops.name: Avenida Hipólito Yrigoyen 370, the arsenal in the basement
stops.date_confidence: 19 July 1975 attested in es.wikipedia, 'Alianza Anticomunista Argentina'. The working notes called this the event that precipitated his fall; it postdates the resignation by eight days and the causality is corrected here
stops.campa: Eight days after the resignation the military finds a weapons arsenal inside the Ministry of Social Welfare. The discovery does not bring him down. He is already down and already out of the country. What it does is confirm what the building was, which is the armoury of the organization the Interior Minister had been saying did not exist. Earlier working notes had the sequence backwards, and the correction is recorded here rather than quietly made.
suggested_refs: The 19 July 1975 arsenal discovery at the Ministerio de Bienestar Social

stops.name: Jerez de la Frontera, the itinerant ambassador
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia places the Jerez residence in 1975 after the July resignation, without a month and without an address; August is the file's placeholder and the residence itself is reconstruction
stops.campa: He settles near Jerez de la Frontera in Andalusia, formally accredited to Spain, formally an ambassador, formally without a task. No address appears in any source consulted. The country he left is run by the president he installed and has eight months before the army takes it. He goes on describing himself in the terms of the book he published in Buenos Aires a few months earlier, a man persecuted by newspapers and vindicated by his own dedication page, in a Spain that is burying Franco.
stops.quote: dentro de ese marco (...) se ha desarrollado la controversial publicidad sobre mi persona y mi vida (…) tratando en todo momento de crearme descrédito y presentarme como un ser repulsivo
stops.quote_source: José López Rega, El idioma de la verdad (1975), quoted in es.wikipedia, 'José López Rega'
suggested_refs: The Spanish residence near Jerez de la Frontera, 1975, address not recorded in any consulted source

stops.name: Madrid, the coup and the request for extradition
stops.date_confidence: 18 June 1976 attested for the junta's extradition request and for the end of the ambassadorial term; the quoted press report is dated 1978 and the search it describes 1979 in the same article, and the two do not agree
stops.campa: The army deposes Isabel Perón in March and the junta it forms asks Spain, on the eighteenth of June, to hand him over. His ambassadorial term ends on that date. The government now hunting him is the one his organization spent three years preparing the ground for, and it wants him for fraud, embezzlement, forgery and criminal association rather than for the dead. Press reports of a search of his Madrid house describe masonic regalia and a shelf of theosophy.
stops.quote: Also found in his home were 12 volumes by Alice Bailey on telepathy and Cosmic Fire.
stops.quote_source: The Times of the Americas (1978), quoted in en.wikipedia, 'José López Rega'
suggested_refs: The Spanish extradition file of 18 June 1976, not reachable

stops.name: Geneva, the first refuge
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia places the flight to Switzerland after the 18 June 1976 extradition request without a month; July is the file's placeholder. en.wikipedia gives an undifferentiated 1975-1982 window between Switzerland and Italy
stops.campa: He crosses into Switzerland and lives near Geneva. English accounts run a loose fugitive window from 1975 to 1982 between Switzerland and Italy without dating the moves; the Spanish account puts Geneva first. Ten years of this begin here, with money whose origin no reachable source explains and a passport whose validity will become the problem that ends the flight. In Buenos Aires the junta is disappearing people at a rate his own organization never reached.
suggested_refs: The Swiss residence near Geneva, 1976 to about 1982, address not recorded

stops.name: Rome, found by the wire service
stops.date_confidence: December 1976 attested for the AFP report locating him in Rome; no day recorded, defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Agence France-Presse reports in December that he is in Rome, sheltered by Italian freemasonry and assisted by Licio Gelli. The lodge he joined in February 1973, weeks before the ministry, is now the thing keeping him out of an Argentine cell. Propaganda Due will not survive the next decade: its membership lists surface in 1981 and take an Italian government down with them. He outlasts the lodge by five years and spends them moving between addresses no journalist prints.
suggested_refs: The Agence France-Presse dispatch of December 1976 locating López Rega in Rome

stops.name: Nassau, the photographed fugitive
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia dates the move to 1983 with an appeals-court reversal as the trigger; en.wikipedia gives 1982-1986 for the Bahamas and Miami period with no trigger. No month recorded, defaulted to 01-01
stops.campa: An appeals court in Argentina overturns an earlier absolution and he leaves Europe for the Bahamas, alternating with Miami for the last three years of the flight. A photographer finds him and publishes, and after that the address is a question of time. The Spanish account supplies the legal trigger and the date; the English account gives a looser window and no trigger. He is sixty-six and has been outside Argentina for eight years, wanted by two governments that succeeded each other.
suggested_refs: The photograph that exposed the Bahamian address, publication not identified in the consulted sources

stops.name: Miami International Airport, the man who introduces himself
stops.date_confidence: 13 March 1986 attested by both encyclopedias, with the warrant dated 27 February 1986. The character of the event is contradicted: es.wikipedia describes a voluntary surrender, en.wikipedia an FBI arrest during a passport renewal. Neither is preferred here
stops.campa: The flight from the Bahamas ends the ten years. The Spanish account has him walking up to the FBI and surrendering on a warrant issued by judge Samuel Smargon on the twenty-seventh of February; the English account has him arrested while trying to renew a passport. Both stand here, because the two encyclopedias describe the same afternoon and do not describe the same act. He is sixty-nine. Argentina has been a democracy again for two years and wants him back.
stops.quote: Mucho gusto. Soy López Rega y vengo a entregarme. Acá están los documentos.
stops.quote_source: Reported words of José López Rega at Miami International Airport, 13 March 1986, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'José López Rega'
suggested_refs: The warrant of judge Samuel Smargon, 27 February 1986, and the FBI record of 13 March 1986, neither consulted

segments.name: The Cell, the Oven, the River

stops.name: Buenos Aires, extradited into preventive detention
stops.date_confidence: 1986 attested for the extradition; no month or day recorded, July is the file's placeholder after the 13 March surrender. The penitentiary unit is named in no consulted source
stops.campa: He is flown back to face charges of criminal association, kidnapping, homicide, fraud, embezzlement and forgery. The country receiving him has just tried its own junta and is learning how to try what came before it. He is held in preventive detention and no source reachable here names the unit. He will stay in it three years without a verdict on any count, which means that the organizer of the Alianza Anticomunista Argentina is never convicted of anything, in that court or in any other.
suggested_refs: The Argentine judicial file on the extradition and preventive detention of 1986, not reachable

stops.name: Buenos Aires, death without a verdict
stops.date_confidence: 9 June 1989 attested in both encyclopedias, with the age of 72 and diabetes mellitus as cause. The facility is not named. The working note that had him awaiting sentence for the murder of Rodolfo Ortega Peña is unsupported and is struck: both sources state there was no completed trial
stops.campa: He dies at seventy-two of complications of diabetes mellitus, in preventive detention, unconvicted. The facility is not named in any source consulted here. The country outside is in hyperinflation and about to hand a presidency over early. Nothing he was charged with has been decided by a court, and nothing he was charged with will ever be decided in his name. He is cremated the next day. The crimes of the organization he built are declared imprescriptible seventeen years later.
suggested_refs: The death certificate of 9 June 1989 and the penitentiary record naming the facility, neither reachable

stops.name: Cementerio de la Chacarita, the oven
stops.date_confidence: the cremation is attested to June 1989 without a day; the day after the death is the file's placeholder. The coordinate is the corpus pin for Chacarita and matches the reference point given in es.wikipedia; the working notes carried two different and both incorrect values
stops.campa: By his own wish the body is cremated at Chacarita, the great secular cemetery the city opened in the yellow fever of 1871, fourteen years after the arsenal in the ministry was found and only months after his extradition from the United States to face charges he did not live to see through to a verdict. No tomb, no stone, no plaque. The man who is said to have kept vigil over another body in a Madrid dining room, and to have worked rites on it through the months it stood there, leaves behind nothing at all that can be visited.
suggested_refs: emin_arslan.journey.json, the Chacarita stop of January 1943, same pin

stops.name: Río de la Plata, the ashes
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1989 without a day. The scattering point is recorded nowhere consulted: the coordinate is an approximation offshore of the city and is not a located place
stops.campa: The ashes go into the river, which is the one thing about the end of this life that everybody agrees on and nobody can locate. No source names the point on the coast, the hour, or who carried them. The coordinate here is an approximation offshore of the city and is marked as one. Between 1976 and 1983 the same water received people dropped from aircraft by the government that succeeded his, which is a fact about the river and not a claim about him.
suggested_refs: The Río de la Plata off Buenos Aires; no scattering point is recorded in any consulted source
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'José López Rega' (the scattering attested, the point reconstructed)

stops.name: Torrente, Valencia, the gunman arrested
stops.date_confidence: 23 December 2006 attested for the Almirón arrest; the Oyarbide ruling is dated 2006 without a day and the convictions to February 2016
stops.campa: Seventeen years after the death, federal judge Norberto Oyarbide rules that the Alliance's crimes are crimes against humanity and therefore cannot expire. Rodolfo Almirón, named as the man who shot Carlos Mugica outside the church at Villa Luro, is arrested in this town near Valencia on the twenty-third of December. In February 2016 four civilians and one police officer are convicted. The organizer has been twenty-seven years dead by then and was never sentenced for anything.
suggested_refs: The 2006 Oyarbide ruling on the imprescriptibility of the Alliance's crimes and the February 2016 convictions
